ui.visit_text: The studio is open by appointment. Please come during opening hours; if nobody answers the door, I am probably in the back room or at the printer's.
ui.commission_text: I take on a small number of commissions each year. When you get in touch, tell me what you have in mind and when you need it, and I will say honestly whether I can do it.
ui.directions: The studio is on the ground floor, a short walk from the town centre. The door is round the side, and there is a bell. Bicycle stands are outside.

photo.intro: Landscape and still-life photography from {city}. Prints and a few commissions each year.
about: I am a photographer working from a small studio in {city}. Most of my pictures are of places in the hour after everyone has left.
I work slowly, usually with one camera and one lens, and print everything myself in the back room. A picture is finished when I can look at it for a week without wanting to change it.
In recent years my work has been shown in small galleries and libraries around the region and sold as prints to people who wanted something quiet for a wall.
services: Fine art prints, signed and numbered
Commissioned portraits at home or in the studio

works.title: Hillside, afternoon
works.caption: Archival pigment print, 2025
works.note: The last of the light on a field that is usually ignored.
works.text: I waited three afternoons for the cloud to lift off the ridge, and it lifted for four minutes.

works.title: Two horizons
works.caption: Archival pigment print, 2025
works.note: A shoreline that could not decide where to end.
works.text: The tide was going out, and the wet sand picked up a second sky. I made six frames and kept this one.

works.title: Quiet water
works.caption: Archival pigment print, 2024
works.note: A pond in November with nothing to prove.
works.text: A reservoir at seven in the morning, before the wind. The print is large, so the stillness has room.

works.title: Red field
works.caption: Archival pigment print, 2024
works.note: Poppies gone to seed, photographed in the rain.
works.text: Clover left to flower and then cut. The colour in the print is closer to what I saw than the camera was.

works.title: Lines at dusk
works.caption: Archival pigment print, 2023
works.note: Telegraph wires against a sky that was changing its mind.
works.text: Fence posts and furrows, with the last light flat across them. It looks better in a long thin frame.

works.title: Salt and slate
works.caption: Archival pigment print, 2023
works.note: A harbour wall at low tide, in the colours of an old coin.
works.text: A beach of dark stone with white salt left by the tide. I came back in three seasons to get the light I wanted.

works.title: Blue hour
works.caption: Archival pigment print, 2022
works.note: Ten minutes between day and night, repeated for a week.
works.text: Ten minutes after sunset the whole valley turns the colour of ink. This is the only frame where the lamp is on.

works.title: Winter orchard
works.caption: Archival pigment print, 2022
works.note: Bare trees in a row, counted twice.
works.text: Bare apple trees on a frosty morning. I stood on a crate to find a line through the branches.

works.title: Morning fog
works.caption: Archival pigment print, 2021
works.note: A valley that had not yet been told it was morning.
works.text: The fog was gone by eight. I made this picture in the quarter of an hour in which it was still there.

illustration.intro: Illustrations, linocuts and small books from a desk in {city}.
about: I am an illustrator and printmaker. I draw for picture books, for magazines that still pay on time, and for anyone who needs a bird in the corner of a poster.
Most of my work begins as a pencil sketch in a notebook and ends as a linocut or a flat-colour digital drawing, whichever the job seems to want.
I live in {city} with a cat who has opinions about my compositions.

shows.t: Field Notes, a picture book from a local press

works.title: Study in orange
works.caption: Linocut, three colours, 2025
works.note: A fox, half a staircase and an unexplained moon.
works.text: A single colour, three papers and an afternoon. It began as a warm-up and became the cover of a small book.

works.title: Market day
works.caption: Digital drawing, 2025
works.note: Eleven stalls and one very smug pigeon.
works.text: Drawn on the spot over three Saturdays. The stallholders were kind enough to keep still, or nearly.

works.title: The long way round
works.caption: Pencil and ink, 2024
works.note: A path that does not go where the sign says.
works.text: A route I walk on Sundays, drawn from memory and then checked on the next walk. The map was wrong in nice ways.

works.title: Night bus
works.caption: Linocut, two colours, 2024
works.note: Everyone is asleep except the driver and the moon.
works.text: Pen, ink and a lot of patience with the reflections in the window.

works.title: Green hours
works.caption: Gouache, 2023
works.note: A greenhouse at four in the afternoon.
works.text: The hours before breakfast in June, when the garden is still cool. Linocut in three colours.

works.title: Small birds
works.caption: Linocut, 2023
works.note: Seven birds, none of them identified correctly.
works.text: Sparrows, wrens and a very cross robin. Each bird is a separate block, so no two prints are exactly alike.

works.title: Rain study
works.caption: Watercolour, 2022
works.note: Umbrellas seen from a window.
works.text: Watercolour, mostly water. I let the paper decide where the puddles went.

works.title: Harvest
works.caption: Digital drawing, 2022
works.note: A field of orange with a tractor in the corner.
works.text: A fruit and vegetable stall in autumn. The orange squash had to be drawn twice.

works.title: Kitchen window
works.caption: Pencil and ink, 2021
works.note: What happens on the sill when nobody is looking.
works.text: The view from where I wash up. It changes with the weather, which is the only reason I do not mind washing up.

graphic.intro: Identities, posters and printed things for small organisations in {city} and beyond.
about: We are a small design studio in {city}. We work with theatres, shops, charities and the occasional brewery, mostly on identities and printed matter.
We like clear grids, honest paper and typefaces that have been around long enough to behave. We try not to make anything that needs a tutorial.
Most projects start with a conversation and a cup of tea, and finish with a box of printed samples on the table.

works.title: Identity for a tea merchant
works.caption: Identity, 2025
works.note: A mark made of one leaf and a great deal of restraint.
works.text: A wordmark, a set of labels and tins that stack. The leaf in the mark is a real leaf from the owner's garden.

works.title: Posters for a choir
works.caption: Poster series, 2025
works.note: Twelve sheets, twelve voices, one grid.
works.text: Three posters for three concerts, printed in two colours on one sheet of paper to keep the cost down.

works.title: Annual report
works.caption: Print, 2024
works.note: Forty pages that people actually read.
works.text: Forty pages for a small charity. Plain type, generous margins and one chart that is allowed to be pretty.

works.title: Programme for a puppet theatre
works.caption: Print, 2024
works.note: Folds into a house and then into a boat.
works.text: A folded sheet that becomes a small theatre when you pull the right corner.

works.title: Packaging for a bakery
works.caption: Packaging, 2023
works.note: Paper bags that look better after one use.
works.text: Paper bags, a stamp and a ribbon in the shop colour. The stamp is cut from a potato.

works.title: Wayfinding for a library
works.caption: Signage, 2023
works.note: Signs that are only noticed when they are missing.
works.text: Signs for four floors, tested with real readers. We moved one sign three times.

works.title: Menu for a small restaurant
works.caption: Print, 2022
works.note: A single sheet that changes every week.
works.text: One page, changed weekly. The layout leaves room for a pen, because the chef always crosses something out.

works.title: Festival poster
works.caption: Poster, 2022
works.note: Printed in two inks on newsprint.
works.text: A poster that had to work from across a street, and it did, thanks to one bold shape and no small print.

works.title: Book cover series
works.caption: Covers, 2021
works.note: Six covers, one typeface.
works.text: Six covers for one publisher, linked by a grid and a single typeface. Each one has its own colour.
